description:
memory.rs:643-655, 736-748, 783-795 — every create/update/destroy in MemoryBackend captures (related_type, type_name) into the ChangeRecord BEFORE the value moves into objects_mut. This is the key invariant that lets get_metadata_changes (the override at memory.rs:835-928) strictly conform to §3.3 — including the destroyed array, which the default-impl post-fetch path cannot filter (the destroyed objects don't exist any more).

The pattern is non-obvious. The naive approach is 'when filtering destroyed, look up the destroyed object's relatedType and @type'. That doesn't work — the object is gone. The capture-at-mutation pattern is the structural insight that lets the override be correct.

This is exactly the kind of pattern a future contributor 'simplifying' would attack: 'why are we storing redundant data in the change log?' Answer: because the change log is the only place this data exists for destroyed entries. The /changes contract requires that the destroyed array supports the same filter as created/updated.

Workspace ref: tracks bd:JMAP-06zp.3.5.2. The override + capture-at-mutation design is the conformance hook for the override path, and is what makes the MemoryBackend reference-grade for §3.3 strict conformance (as advertised in metadata.rs:55-56 and README.md line 8-10).

Defend against: 'denormalize the change log', 'just look up the object', 'this is duplicating state'. The duplication is load-bearing for the destroyed-array filter contract.

Adjacent: the related smell of empty-string sentinels for non-Metadata types (JMAP-ayoz.11) — fixing that should not erode this invariant. The capture-at-mutation must remain unconditional for Metadata records.
title: MemoryBackend.get_metadata_changes captures (related_type, type_name) at mutation time
